entities.summary:
The Battle of Messana was the first military conflict between the Roman Republic and Carthage, marking the start of the First Punic War and a pivotal moment in the ancient Mediterranean world. 

 This decisive battle took place in 263 BCE in Messina, a strategic location at the northeastern tip of Sicily, and was a turning point in the struggle for control of the Mediterranean. 

 The Roman victory led to a prolonged conflict with Carthage, which would shape the course of Western history for centuries to come. 

 As the Roman Republic expanded its dominion over the Mediterranean, the legacy of the Battle of Messana continued to resonate, inspiring future generations of politicians, soldiers, and historians.
